summary.oneLiner: Schaeffler India is a leading motion technology company operating at the intersection of engineering, mobility transformation, industrial productivity and sustainability, serving automotive and industrial customers through three divisions.
summary.business: Schaeffler India, part of the Schaeffler Group with over 80 years of motion-technology heritage, designs and manufactures precision-engineered components and system solutions spanning automotive and industrial applications. Its portfolio blends mechanical engineering with electronics and software across Automotive Technologies (E-Mobility, Powertrain and Chassis), Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (aftermarket repair and service), and Bearings & Industrial Solutions (rolling and plain bearings, linear and direct-drive technologies).

Automotive Technologies: Hybrid, fully electric and fuel-cell mobility solutions
Vehicle Lifetime Solutions: Clutch, engine, transmission and chassis repair solutions
Bearings & Industrial Solutions: Rolling and plain bearings (compact high-speed to large-scale)

endMarkets: Passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles (automotive OEMs)|Two-wheelers (including electric two-wheelers)|Off-road / industrial equipment|Aftermarket garages and workshops (via KOOVERS and distribution network)|Industrial and general engineering|Exports

risks.risk: Climate transition and physical climate risk to cost base and supply chain
risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table flags emissions management as a risk: carbon pricing mandates and regulatory compliance raise operational costs, and policy direction toward low-carbon manufacturing 'may necessitate capital investments and operational changes'. Physically, storms, floods and heatwaves 'could have significant direct and indirect impact on our supply chain and operations, potentially disrupting production and affecting our ability to fulfill demand'. The Company also states it depends on suppliers, primarily in the steel sector, to develop lower-carbon alternatives to control the carbon footprint embedded in its products - i.e. a cost driver it does not control. All manufacturing sites have undergone structured climate risk assessments and climate considerations are embedded into capital expenditure decisions.

risks.risk: Product quality, safety and regulatory non-compliance risk in OEM supply
risks.note: Schaeffler India sells into automotive and industrial customers that demand high standards of quality, safety, regulatory compliance and environmental performance; the AR states product quality and safety 'are critical to maintaining customer trust and long-term OEM relationships'. Disclosed downside is recalls, warranty claims, safety incidents, regulatory penalties and reputational damage, mitigated through group-wide product validation and approval processes and a 'zero-defect' culture. The same row concedes incremental capex and opex on R&D and design is required to stay compliant with evolving material-compliance, hazardous-substance and end-of-life requirements.

risks.risk: Occupational safety exposure across shop floor and contract workforce
risks.note: Listed in the BRSR table as a pure Risk. Manufacturing operations 'involve significant engagement of employees and contract workers on the shop floor'; lapses could cause injuries, downtime and non-financial impacts 'that are not easily reversible'. Financial exposure named: medical expenses, compensation payments, regulatory penalties, litigation costs, higher insurance premiums and production downtime. The Company notes the nature of operations limits exposure to highly hazardous substances, so the exposure is accident/continuity-driven rather than process-chemical.

risks.risk: Cyber and data-security risk across ERP, order management and customer engineering data
risks.note: Listed as a pure Risk. Increasing digitalisation of enterprise systems - specifically ERP, order management and customer-specific engineering data - means a breach could expose sensitive commercial, technical or personal information, disrupt operations, breach data-protection regulation and 'impact long-term customer trust and OEM relationships'. Mitigation is an IT governance framework supported by Group-wide information security (the disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the routed text), so the control environment is inherited from the parent rather than standalone.

risks.risk: Input price volatility, import dependence and supplier capacity constraints
risks.note: The procurement disclosure states localisation 'is at the heart of our strategy' precisely to 'reduce dependence on imports, enhance supply reliability, and respond swiftly to customers', and that the dual-sourcing approach and long-term agreements 'help mitigate risks from price volatility, capacity constraints, and external disruptions'. That is an explicit admission of three live structural exposures - imported input dependence, raw-material/component price volatility, and supplier capacity - in a business whose procurement framework must simultaneously balance cost efficiency against quality, supply consistency and ESG qualification. Sustainable sourcing is reported at 60%.

risks.risk: Dependence on the Schaeffler Group parent for technology, validation and shared frameworks
risks.note: Product development is explicitly 'aligned with Schaeffler Group's global R&D agenda', product approval runs through 'group-wide product validation and approval processes', and information security is Group-wide - so the India entity's innovation pipeline and key control frameworks are set outside it. The AR also records that following the Group's merger with Vitesco Technologies the SBTi-validated climate targets 'are currently under review', showing India-level commitments can be reset by parent-level corporate action. Reporting scope reinforces the dependence: performance data relate to Schaeffler India Limited, with Group references included only 'for strategic context'.

risks.risk: Concentrated board control by parent nominees alongside heavy directorship churn
risks.note: The 2025 at a Glance governance panel discloses only 38% Independent Directors. During 2025-early 2026 the AR records repeated turnover at committee level: Amit Kalyani resigned from the Board and ceased as NRC Chairperson effective July 23, 2025; Dharmesh Arora ceased as NRC member effective May 31, 2025; Andreas Schick ceased from both the Audit Committee and the Risk Management Committee effective February 24, 2026. Chairmanship of the Risk Management Committee passed from Harsha Kadam to Maximilian Andreas Fiedler, a Non-Executive Non-Independent (parent-nominee) director, effective February 7, 2026 - placing oversight of the enterprise risk framework with a non-independent director.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Automotive Technologies demand supported by recent GST reforms and record festive sales, reflecting robust consumer demand and a recovering market, against ongoing challenges from rare earth materials controls, tariff-driven demand uncertainty and persistent semiconductor shortages.
- GST reforms have stimulated demand growth in passenger vehicles, MHCVs and tractors.
- India's automotive aftermarket (Vehicle Lifetime Solutions) remains structurally attractive, supported by a large and ageing vehicle parc, high vehicle utilisation across segments, strong demand for cost-efficient maintenance solutions, and increasing formalisation of distribution channels.
- India's vehicle parc continues to expand structurally across passenger vehicles, tractors and commercial vehicles; aftermarket ecosystem is formalising and digital channels are gaining relevance.
- India's GDP growth outlook for FY2025-26 revised upward by RBI to 7.3% (from 6.8%), driven by robust domestic demand, income tax and GST rationalisation, softer crude oil prices, and front-loaded government capital expenditure.
- India surpassed Japan in 2025 to become the world's fourth-largest economy (GDP USD 4.18 trillion) and is on a path to become the third-largest economy by 2030 (projected GDP USD 7.3 trillion), supporting a strategic landscape for localised manufacturing and industrial innovation.
- Global growth estimated at 2.7% in 2025 with IMF projecting 3.3% for 2026, aided by technology investment, fiscal/monetary support and easing financial conditions, though global trade outlook remains dampened by tariff-policy uncertainty.
- Nomination by a global original equipment manufacturer of transmission components to meet global and domestic requirements, reinforcing Schaeffler India's role as a strategic global hub for ICE powertrain components.
- Business wins for engine cam phasing systems supporting a key customer's ICE powertrain strategy focused on regulatory compliance and fuel efficiency.
- Capitalised on emerging CAFE norms by delivering tailored solutions to help customers comply with upcoming emission regulations across PV and CV segments.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Subsidiary] KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions Private Limited is a loss-making consolidation drag — on 791 mn INR of Q2 2026 revenue it posted a -17.3% EBITDA and -19.1% EBIT margin, pulling consolidated EBITDA margin to 18.5% from 19.1% standalone.
- [Cost headwind] Management attributes the marginal decline in earnings quality to geopolitical developments, specifically fuel prices and a depreciating INR, rather than to pricing or mix.
- [CSR] The company was recognised in the Tribal and Indigenous Communities Development category at the CSR Convention and Best Practices in CSR Awards 2026, indicating community-development programmes as its main disclosed CSR thrust.
- [Sourcing] Sandvik Mining and Rock Technology India recognised the company with an Agile, Customer-Focused Cost Excellence and Efficient Sourcing award, the deck's only signal on cost and sourcing capability.
